gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states that Lofree's own spec sheets call both of its 100-key low-profile boards (Flow Lite 2 100, Flow 2 100) a 96% layout with no Linux in the compatible-systems list, while Keychron lists the K5 Max as 100% / 108 keys for macOS, Windows and Linux with hot-swap on only one of its three backlight versions.
standout_why: Compared against the RTINGS low-profile roundup (updated 2026-10-09), the RTINGS K5 Max review and purchase.fyi (2026-02-28). RTINGS's roundup gives only 1,000 Hz wired/2.4 GHz for the K5 Max and names the Air100 V3 as the numpad option; its review says a hot-swappable PCB is an option and three devices pair, but the OS, keycap and polling rows were locked in the copy I could read. purchase.fyi already has the 90 Hz Bluetooth figure and 'Gateron LP and NuPhy LP' sockets for the K3 Max and says the K5 Max shares them, so those two points are only part-new. None of the three gives the maker's layout percentage or key count for the Lofree 100-key boards, the Lofree OS list, the K5 Ultra 8K's per-mode polling and ZMK firmware, the optical-switch exclusion, or the Flow100 discontinuation. Not read: technobezz.com (HTTP 403), the RTINGS G915 X LIGHTSPEED review body (page returned navigation only) and the other results in the list, so the 'no result' claim covers only the three pages named here.
decides: It decides whether a Lofree row belongs. ChatGPT's second answer explicitly excluded 'a compressed 96% keyboard that happens to include a numpad', and Lofree itself labels the Flow Lite 2 100 and Flow 2 100 as 96% / 100 keys; they pass this page's 98-108-key line only on key count, so the row must say '100 keys, 96% by Lofree's own figure'. On maker-stated compatibility the Keychron K5 Max (108 keys, Linux listed, QMK) and K5 Ultra 8K (100%, 8,000 Hz wired and 2.4 GHz) stay ahead for a shopper who wants a true 100% layout; Lofree's honest segment is the lighter, shorter 100-key board for Mac/Windows users who don't need Linux. Two cautions for any Lofree row: the Flow100 is discontinued (final US units, Bluetooth and USB-C only per our record) and the Flow Lite 2 100 page carried a 'Ships from Dec 1' line. A buyer who wants to change switches on the K5 Max must order the 'RGB Backlight (Hot-Swappable)' version, and both Keychrons fall to 90-125 Hz on Bluetooth.
